head: 0b56a0f70b335cb7f54ae3974fb08d899c26ec1f
summary: The size probe now opens a file a second time when the first open fails with ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE (1920). In SizeProbe.Probe, that error triggers one call to a new SynchronousIoCancel.OpenReparsePointForAttributes, which is the same cancellable CreateFileW open with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT added. The file is then sized from that handle's FileStandardInfo, and if the second open fails, its error is what gets reported. No other error is retried, and OpenForAttributes still opens with flags 0. I added the two constants to Kernel32.cs, a per-instance test hook (OverrideReparseRetryError) that fakes a refused retry, an APPEXECLINK plant in the test fixtures, and ten Facts plus one four-row Theory in the new ReparsePointProbeTests.cs. I also rewrote fitness rules A and B as the review asked (m2, m3). Results: the acceptance repro now exits 0, all 425 Core.Tests pass, and the engine's own fitness check reports no violations. Run through the shipped Core on this PC's real folders, probe failures under WindowsApps fell from 114 to 0, and across the user profile from 238 to 119; the 119 left are consistent with the cloud files the spike found failing with 363, which stay counted by design.

files.why: Adds FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT (0x00200000) and ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE (1920) next to the existing constants. No new P/Invoke.

New OpenReparsePointForAttributes: the same private Open (CreateFileW, FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, share all, same bracket, same thread) with the reparse-point flag. New per-instance test hook OverrideReparseRetryError (review M2, modelled on OverrideQueryError as the person decided). Comments rewritten: the flag is not used on the first open, and a folder's 1920 is never retried.
Probe retries once, only on 1920, through OpenReparsePointForAttributes, and returns the retry's error if that fails. Comments updated, including review m7's accepted dedup-without-filter wording.
Default-suite Facts on real %TEMP% trees for design cases 1-7 and the M2 failed-retry branch.
SetReparsePoint (FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT, takes the tag as a parameter), in the one test file InteropLivesOnlyInNative allows.
AppExecAlias(relative, length): writes a file of N bytes and plants tag 0x8000001B over it.

Rules A and B under '# settled by SL-084' rewritten per the accepted review findings m2 and m3: Kernel32.cs added to except_files, lookaheads dropped, the decimal (2097152) and 0x780 spellings covered. A comment records why. No xUnit twin, as with the other settled entries.

obligations.how: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-084-ReparseProbeRetry/SL-084-ReparseProbeRetry.Tests.csproj exited 0, with 1 of 1 passed. The repro is unchanged.

Read SL-056 rule 3 at .taad/fitness.yaml:704-712. It covers Scanning/*.cs and its only pattern is (?m)\bNtOpenFile\b, so it says nothing about the flag. I left it untouched; the retry is still CreateFileW through the private Open. I ran the engine's taad3.fitness.check on a scratch copy with the retry in place: 65 rules, 0 violations. The verdict was 'unable' only because the one import rule cannot run on a scratch copy, which has no code graph.

ReparsePointProbeTests.AnAfUnixSocketBoundForTheWholeScanIsSizedFromItsOwnHandle keeps the socket bound for the whole scan and disposes it before the TempTree. It asserts the listing shows the reparse bit and tag 0x80000023, the first open returns 1920, the entry is a File that is SizeProbed and not ProbeFailed, and Probes/ProbeFailures are 2/0. It fails with the retry disabled.

ReparsePointProbeTests.AnAppExecutionAliasInAScannedTreeIsSizedFromItsOwnHandle plants tag 0x8000001B over 5000 bytes with FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT. It asserts the listed tag, the first open returning 1920, flags exactly SizeProbed, size 5000, ProbeFailures 0 and total bytes 5100. It fails with the retry disabled.

NTFS does accept the plant on a non-empty file: measured on 12345 bytes, unelevated. ReparsePointProbeTests.AProbeOfAnAliasOverNBytesReadsTheRetriedHandlesSizes asserts Probe returns 0, io.Calls is 3 (first open, retry, query), EndOfFile equals N, and AllocationSize equals the listing's. It fails with the retry disabled.

ReparsePointProbeTests.TheFirstOpenOfAnAliasStillFailsAndOnlyTheRetryOpensIt asserts OpenForAttributes returns 1920 with a null handle, and OpenReparsePointForAttributes returns 0 with a valid handle. This pins the first open at flags 0.

ReparsePointProbeTests.AFileWhoseFirstOpenSucceedsIsNeverRetried covers a plain file (Probe gives 0, EndOfFile 10, exactly 2 calls) and a WOF-compressed file (2 calls, allocation below its size, so the filter answered). The full Core.Tests suite (425) is also green, including the 106 probe, cancel and long-path tests.

ReparsePointProbeTests.APlainFileRefusedBySynchronizeDenyIsNotRetriedAndStaysProbeFailed denies SYNCHRONIZE only (SL-045). Probe returns 5 after exactly 1 call, so there is no retry. The scan shows ProbeFailed, ProbeFailures 1 and the listing size kept. The existing OnDiskSizeTests wof-denied.txt refusal Fact also stays green.

Measured first: on an alias under a SYNCHRONIZE deny (and under S|RA), the first open still returns 1920 and it is the retry that returns 5. ReparsePointProbeTests.AnAliasRefusedBySynchronizeDenyFailsItsRetryAndStaysProbeFailed asserts that pair exactly and reports both codes in its message, rather than accepting either outcome. It also asserts Probe returns 5, not 1920, and that the scan entry is exactly ProbeFailed and counted, with its listing size kept.

I added a per-instance hook, SynchronousIoCancel.OverrideReparseRetryError, consulted only by OpenReparsePointForAttributes. It closes any handle the retry did open and refuses to turn a failure into a success. This follows the person's decision to use the OverrideQueryError pattern, not the static SL-082 failpoint. ReparsePointProbeTests.ARetryThatFailsReportsItsOwnError has rows for 2, 3, 5 and 32. Directly, Probe returns that error with zero sizes, the hook saw a real successful retry (0), and a plain file never reaches the hook. Through a scan with a ScanOptions.Probe wrapper, 2 and 3 count as gone (VanishedBeforeProbe 1, flags None, not counted), while 5 and 32 are ProbeFailed and counted. The case-7 part is covered under O-009.

Rule A now uses must_not_match \bFILE_(FLAG_)?OPEN_REPARSE_POINT\b and \b(?:0x0*200000|2097152)[uU]?\b, with except_files Kernel32.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs. In a scratch copy, the engine flagged a planted redefinition in SizeProbe.cs (twice) and a named-argument 2097152 plus a hex local in Scanner.cs. The real tree has 0 hits.

Rule B now uses must_not_match \bERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE\b and \b(?:1920|0x0*780)\b, with except_files Kernel32.cs and SizeProbe.cs. The baseline grep of src found no bare 1920 or 0x780 in code outside those files; the SynchronousIoCancel.cs mentions are comments, which the engine does not match. In a scratch copy, the engine flagged a planted 'e is 5 or 1920' and '== 0x780' in Scanner.cs and '!= Kernel32.ERROR_CANT_ACCESS_FILE' in MainWindow.xaml.cs. The real tree has 0 hits.

Recorded as accepted, not guarded, in SizeProbe.Probe's remarks. A dedup-optimized file on a volume with no dedup filter takes the retry and is sized from its stub, the same figures its listing gives; only the 'could not be opened' note changes. WOF and cloud never reach the retry. There is no FileAttributeTagInfo check. The code's rationale for having no gate is 'keyed on the error, not on a tag' and does not cite U-004. The design record, where the U-004 citation sits, is not in this repository, so I could not correct it.

The bound-socket Fact asserts, before scanning, that OpenForAttributes on s.sock returns exactly 1920 under testhost. It passed, so testhost does get 1920 for a bound AF_UNIX socket file, and the socket Fact cannot pass without the retry running.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.ReparsePointProbeTests.<each case's method>"

deviations: The design said the alias plant 'reuses or extends the suite's existing reparse/junction native helper'. There is none: junctions and hardlinks are made by running cmd.exe mklink (TempTree.Run), and TestNative.cs had only FSCTL_SET_SPARSE. I added TestNative.SetReparsePoint (a DeviceIoControl overload that takes a byte[] and the tag as a parameter), inside the one test file InteropLivesOnlyInNative allows, plus TempTree.AppExecAlias.

The design said 'the existing ProbePassTests refusal Facts' cover case 6. ProbePassTests holds no ACL refusal Fact. The existing one is OnDiskSizeTests' wof-denied.txt, a WOF file denied SYNCHRONIZE|RA. So I added APlainFileRefusedBySynchronizeDenyIsNotRetriedAndStaysProbeFailed to feed exactly the case's shape (a plain file, SYNCHRONIZE-only deny) and pin it to one open.
follow_ups: The schema-1 --report (WindowReport.cs) carries neither ScanResult.ProbeFailures nor the OutcomeNotes text, so the 'N files could not be opened to read their true size on disk' note cannot be observed through the shipped exe's report. Design case 14 expected validate to 'run this through --report and expect 0 probe failures'; that is not measurable today, and a no-retry exe gives an identical report. Adding core.probeFailures (and vanishedBeforeProbe) or OutcomeNotes to the report is an App change for its own slice. Until then, the only way to observe C4 on real input is the Core-level measurement recorded under tests (WindowsApps 114 -> 0, profile 238 -> 119).
